metadata.title: Checks the Picture, Then Stops.
metadata.subtitle: The FSI-Strip-Profile Skill (Anthropic Skills)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude runs an Anthropic Skill like fsi-strip-profile, does it just trust the slide it built, or does it check its own work first? Lands the carry-out that the skill makes Claude render its own slide to a picture and inspect it — then stop and wait for your approval — before it ever shows you one, one slide at a time.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed Claude trusts the slide it just built. It doesn't — it turns it into a picture and checks first. So: does Claude check the strip profile it builds?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW fix (this build): first attempt used a 69-char text against a 9.34s narration and the typing did not finish before the clip ended (caught by frame pull at t=9.1s: 'the slide it buil|', missing 't?'). remotion_scenes.py sets B00's render duration directly from actual_duration_s (audio length) — lead_silence_s is NOT added to the render duration by this script, so the fix is a shorter on-screen text (46 chars) rather than a longer lead_silence_s. Re-verified by frame pull after the fix. NOTE: remotion_scenes.py's own extend_clip_to_duration step reported success ('extended to 9.0s') but the resulting media/B00.mp4 was actually the raw 20.2s render (the ffmpeg trim/pad call inside that function did not overwrite the output, and the script does not check its own ffmpeg call's exit code before claiming success). Verified by ffprobe (20.245s, contradicting the actual_duration_s=9.02 stamp), then fixed by re-running the same tpad+trim ffmpeg command manually (exit 0, confirmed 9.033s output) and installing that in place of the raw render.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is fsi-strip-profile. The SKILL.md file inside it is the full instruction set — plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.
First it asks: one slide or several, and what to focus on. Only once you say yes does it start digging into filings, market data, and recent news.

Then it builds one slide at a time. After each one, it turns the slide into a picture and looks for text spilling out, labels cut off, a chart bleeding into the next box. It fixes what it finds — then shows you the slide and stops, waiting for your yes before the next one.
Inside this skill, Claude checks its own picture before it ever shows you one — then it stops. That's what makes each slide something you actually approved, not just something the model produced.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I want a one-slide investment profile for Nike, ticker N-K-E. Read the fsi-strip-profile skill and walk me through what you will do — including how you'll check the slide — before you build it. That last clause matters — asking Claude to explain the check first is what actually shows you the picture it's about to look at.
